title: C2OPU: Hybrid Compute-in-Memory and Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Architecture for Overlay Processing of Transformers
problem: Von Neumann architecture-based accelerators are memory-bound when processing Transformers, and computing-in-memory (CIM) processors suffer from computing pattern mismatches and low precision that limit transformer acceleration effectiveness.
motivation: Efficient hardware acceleration is critical for increasingly large Transformer models in NLP applications where memory bandwidth is a bottleneck.
method: C2OPU is a hybrid dual-core processor combining CIM arrays for weight-stationary vector-matrix multiplications with a coarse-grained reconfigurable architecture (CGRA) to handle computing pattern mismatches and precision limitations. An accuracy-bound workload allocation strategy balances throughput and accuracy by considering non-ideal analog computing characteristics. A compiler automatically determines optimal system configurations when transformer models change.
key_novelty: Hybrid architecture coupling CIM for efficient matrix operations with CGRA for flexible high-precision computation, enabled by accuracy-bound workload allocation and automated compilation.
contributions: Dual-core hybrid architecture combining CIM arrays and CGRA to overcome computing pattern mismatch and precision limitations
Accuracy-bound workload allocation strategy accounting for non-ideal analog computing characteristics
Compiler framework for automatic system configuration optimization across different transformer models
Comprehensive experimental validation on ten transformer models with significant speedups over CPU, GPU, and prior art

metrics.speedup: 145.41× vs CPU, 4.73× vs GPU, 4.70× vs Science23, 3.85× vs Nature23, 1.37× vs VLSI24
